key_insight: RecursiveMAS shows that multi-agent collaboration can be scaled by letting agents iteratively refine a shared latent state in a recursive loop, effectively turning the whole agent system into a deeper reasoning process.
problem_solved: Existing recursive/looped reasoning techniques were applied to single models; this work addresses whether and how recursion can scale coordination and collective reasoning in heterogeneous multi-agent systems.
method: Cast the multi-agent system as a unified latent-space computation where agents read and write to shared latent state across iterations.
Run recursive update loops: agents iteratively refine their contributions to latent state and each other's outputs to deepen joint reasoning.
Support heterogeneous agents and communication protocols within the same recursive framework to improve collective decision-making and task performance.
impact: Provides a new scaling axis for multi-agent systems that improves collaborative reasoning and complex problem solving by repeatedly refining shared internal representations; useful for designing more capable, coordinated AI teams.
visual_elements: Diagram of RecursiveMAS loop: multiple heterogeneous agents around a shared latent-state memory with arrows showing iterative read/write cycles.
Before vs. After chart: performance or reasoning-depth comparison between single-pass multi-agent and recursive multi-agent runs.
Flowchart of a single recursion step: agent inputs → latent update → agent outputs → next iteration.
Icon set: heterogeneous agent avatars (e.g., planner, critic, generator) connected to a central latent-state node.
paper_authors: Xiyuan Yang, Jiaru Zou, Rui Pan, Ruizhong Qiu, Pan Lu
